source_text: וַ/תִּקַּ֧ח הָֽ/אִשָּׁ֛ה אֶת שְׁנֵ֥י הָ/אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַֽ/תִּצְפְּנ֑/וֹ וַ/תֹּ֣אמֶר כֵּ֗ן בָּ֤אוּ אֵלַ/י֙ הָֽ/אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְ/לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי מֵ/אַ֥יִן הֵֽמָּה־׀׃
english_snapshot: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them[a], and she said, “Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.”

signals.text: Hebrew has a singular suffix in 'and hid him' (וַתִּצְפְּנוֹ), but the context refers to the two men collectively; hence 'hidden them.'

source_text: וַ/יַּעַמְד֡וּ הַ/מַּיִם֩ הַ/יֹּרְדִ֨ים מִ/לְ/מַ֜עְלָ/ה קָ֣מוּ נֵד אֶחָ֗ד הַרְחֵ֨ק מְאֹ֜ד ב/אדם הָ/עִיר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִ/צַּ֣ד צָֽרְתָ֔ן וְ/הַ/יֹּרְדִ֗ים עַ֣ל יָ֧ם הָ/עֲרָבָ֛ה יָם הַ/מֶּ֖לַח תַּ֣מּוּ נִכְרָ֑תוּ וְ/הָ/עָ֥ם עָבְר֖וּ נֶ֥גֶד יְרִיחֽוֹ־־׃
english_snapshot: the waters flowing down from above stood still[a]; they rose up in one heap, very far away, at Adam, the city beside Zarethan. And those flowing down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off[b], and the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

signals.text: 'The Salt Sea' is the body of water later commonly called the Dead Sea.

source_text: וַ/יְהִ֣י כִ/שְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּל מַלְכֵ֣י הָ/אֱמֹרִ֡י אֲשֶׁר֩ בְּ/עֵ֨בֶר הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֜ן יָ֗מָּ/ה וְ/כָל מַלְכֵ֤י הַֽ/כְּנַעֲנִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַ/יָּ֔ם אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת מֵ֧י הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֛ן מִ/פְּנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד עבר/נו וַ/יִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבָ֗/ם וְ/לֹא הָ֨יָה בָ֥/ם עוֹד֙ ר֔וּחַ מִ/פְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל־־־־־־־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: And it happened[a], when all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan to the west, and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea, heard that Yahweh had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the sons of Israel until we had crossed over, their heart melted[c][b], and there was no longer spirit in them because of the sons of Israel.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and ancient versions read 'until they had crossed over' instead of 'until we had crossed over.'

source_text: כִּ֣י אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה הָלְכ֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ בַּ/מִּדְבָּר֒ עַד תֹּ֨ם כָּל הַ/גּ֜וֹי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַ/מִּלְחָמָה֙ הַ/יֹּצְאִ֣ים מִ/מִּצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּ/ק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לָ/הֶ֔ם לְ/בִלְתִּ֞י הַרְאוֹתָ֣/ם אֶת הָ/אָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה לַֽ/אֲבוֹתָ/ם֙ לָ֣/תֶת לָ֔/נוּ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּ/דְבָֽשׁ׀־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: For the sons of Israel had walked in the wilderness forty years[a], until all the nation—the men of war who came out of Egypt—had come to an end, because they had not listened to the voice of Yahweh. Yahweh had sworn to them that he would not let them see the land that Yahweh had sworn to their fathers to give to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'to give to us'; some ancient versions and translations read 'to give to them.'

english_snapshot: Then Joshua returned[a], and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

signals.text: A similar return-to-Gilgal statement appears in Joshua 10:43; some interpreters view this verse as anticipatory or textually displaced, but the Hebrew text here is translated as it stands.

source_text: וְ/הָ/עֲרָבָה֩ עַד יָ֨ם כִּנְר֜וֹת מִזְרָ֗חָ/ה וְ֠/עַד יָ֣ם הָ/עֲרָבָ֤ה יָם הַ/מֶּ֨לַח֙ מִזְרָ֔חָ/ה דֶּ֖רֶךְ בֵּ֣ית הַיְשִׁמ֑וֹת וּ/מִ֨/תֵּימָ֔ן תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדּ֥וֹת הַ/פִּסְגָּֽה־־׃
english_snapshot: and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Kinnereth eastward[a], and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, by way of Beth-jeshimoth, and southward[b], below the slopes of Pisgah.

signals.text: 'The Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea' refers to what is later commonly called the Dead Sea.

source_text: וַ/יְהִ֤י לָ/הֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל נֶ֔גֶב מִ/קְצֵ֖ה יָ֣ם הַ/מֶּ֑לַח מִן הַ/לָּשֹׁ֖ן הַ/פֹּנֶ֥ה נֶֽגְבָּ/ה־׃
english_snapshot: Their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea[b][a], from the tongue that faces southward.

signals.text: Some English versions read 'Balah' here, likely influenced by parallel town lists; the Masoretic Text reads Baalah.

source_text: וְ/שַׁעֲרַ֨יִם֙ וַ/עֲדִיתַ֔יִם וְ/הַ/גְּדֵרָ֖ה וּ/גְדֵרֹתָ֑יִם עָרִ֥ים אַרְבַּֽע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה וְ/חַצְרֵי/הֶֽן־׃
english_snapshot: and Shaaraim[a], and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim: fourteen cities with their villages.

signals.text: Some interpreters note that the four place names listed in this verse do not obviously total the stated 'fourteen cities'; the larger section's textual history may account for the discrepancy, but the Hebrew text here is translated as given.

source_text: וְ/עָבַ֨ר הַ/גְּב֜וּל אֶל כֶּ֣תֶף בֵּית חָגְלָה֮ צָפוֹנָ/ה֒ ו/היה תצאותי/ו הַ/גְּב֗וּל אֶל לְשׁ֤וֹן יָם הַ/מֶּ֨לַח֙ צָפ֔וֹנָ/ה אֶל קְצֵ֥ה הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֖ן נֶ֑גְבָּ/ה זֶ֖ה גְּב֥וּל נֶֽגֶב־־׀־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then the border passed to the northern shoulder of Beth-hoglah[a], and the border ended at the northern tongue of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan[b]. This is the southern border.

signals.text: Or 'the Dead Sea'; the Hebrew text reads 'the Salt Sea.'

source_text: וְ/צֵלַ֡ע הָאֶ֜לֶף וְ/הַ/יְבוּסִ֨י הִ֤יא יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ גִּבְעַ֣ת קִרְיַ֔ת עָרִ֥ים אַרְבַּֽע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה וְ/חַצְרֵי/הֶ֑ן זֹ֛את נַֽחֲלַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי בִנְיָמִ֖ן לְ/מִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽ/ם־־׃פ
english_snapshot: Zela[a], Haeleph, the Jebusite (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeath, Kiriath—fourteen cities with their villages[c][b]. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin according to their clans.

signals.text: The Hebrew text reads 'Kiriath,' not 'Kiriath-jearim' in this verse.

source_text: וַ/יְהִ֥י לָ/הֶ֖ם בְּ/נַֽחֲלָתָ֑/ם בְּאֵֽר שֶׁ֥בַע וְ/שֶׁ֖בַע וּ/מוֹלָדָֽה־׃
english_snapshot: And they had in their inheritance Beer-sheba[a], Sheba, and Moladah.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Beer-sheba and Sheba.' Some understand this as a single place name ('Beer-sheba') with a textual or stylistic irregularity rather than two separate towns.

source_text: וּ/בֵ֥ית לְבָא֖וֹת וְ/שָֽׁרוּחֶ֑ן עָרִ֥ים שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה וְ/חַצְרֵי/הֶֽן־׃
english_snapshot: Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen cities[a], with their villages.

signals.text: Hebrew Sharuhen; Joshua 15:32 has the variant name Shilhim in a parallel list.

source_text: וְ/עֶבְרֹ֥ן וּ/רְחֹ֖ב וְ/חַמּ֣וֹן וְ/קָנָ֑ה עַ֖ד צִיד֥וֹן רַבָּֽה׃
english_snapshot: Ebron[a], Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Ebron'; some textual traditions and translations read 'Abdon.'

source_text: וְ/שָׁ֨ב הַ/גְּב֥וּל יָ֨מָּ/ה֙ אַזְנ֣וֹת תָּב֔וֹר וְ/יָצָ֥א מִ/שָּׁ֖ם חוּקֹ֑קָ/ה וּ/פָגַ֨ע בִּ/זְבֻל֜וּן מִ/נֶּ֗גֶב וּ/בְ/אָשֵׁר֙ פָּגַ֣ע מִ/יָּ֔ם וּ/בִ֣/יהוּדָ֔ה הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֖ן מִזְרַ֥ח הַ/שָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
english_snapshot: Then the border turned westward to Aznoth-tabor[a], and from there it went out to Hukkok, and it reached Zebulun on the south, and it reached Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the east, where the sun rises.

signals.text: Hebrew 'and Judah at the Jordan toward the east.' The geography is difficult, since Naphtali did not directly border the tribal territory of Judah in the usual sense. Some understand the wording differently or suspect textual difficulty, but the Hebrew text is translated as it stands.

source_text: וּ/מִֽ/מַּחֲצִית֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אֶת תַּעְנַךְ֙ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֔/הָ וְ/אֶת גַּת רִמּ֖וֹן וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֑/הָ עָרִ֖ים שְׁתָּֽיִם־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasturelands[a], and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands—two cities.

signals.text: Some Hebrew manuscripts and the parallel in 1 Chronicles 6:70 differ in the names of the towns assigned from Manasseh.

source_text: אֶת דִּמְנָה֙ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֔/הָ אֶֽת נַהֲלָ֖ל וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֑/הָ עָרִ֖ים אַרְבַּֽע־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Dimnah with its pasturelands[b][a], and Nahalal with its pasturelands—four cities.

signals.text: Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions differ on the inclusion and arrangement of some city names in this section; compare the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 6:62 [English 6:77].

source_text: וּ/מִ/מַּטֵּ֣ה רְאוּבֵ֔ן אֶת בֶּ֖צֶר וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֑/הָ וְ/אֶת יַ֖הְצָ/ה וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶֽׁ/הָ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasturelands[b][a], and Jahaz with its pasturelands.

signals.text: Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient witnesses omit Joshua 21:36–37; the cities listed here parallel 1 Chronicles 6:78–79.
